description:
Functional specifications covered with associated files to edit/add: Connect.refresh_grant/resolve_bearer_token/update_grant_token_cache, existing OAuth refresh implementation and scheduled refresh worker, CredentialResolver integration, concurrency tests under test/zaq/engine/connect/ and worker tests. Reuse existing refresh mechanisms, reload grant and credential before use, never refresh revoked/deleted rows from stale structs. Use per-grant single-flight claim or versioned compare-and-swap around external call; no transaction lock held across network IO. Persist returned tokens only if grant/status/config version still matches. Replacement/revocation/deletion wins over in-flight stale refresh; discard stale returned secrets, never resurrect authorization. Coordinate scheduled and resolver-triggered refresh. Preserve provider refresh_token when omitted by successful response, rotate when supplied. Successful persisted refresh emits same durable credential/person mutation event, failed refresh never triggers global fallback. Resolver refreshes selected OAuth grant when appropriate then returns latest authentication; policy selected once for this resolution, not on every future runtime request. Define expires_at/status versus usable refresh-token semantics explicitly: revoked always terminal; expired with valid refresh material may recover; expired without recoverable refresh yields structured authentication-required/expired error. Errors sanitize provider bodies. Avoid unrestricted retries under shared expired grant; bound refresh attempts and expose retryable failure distinctly.

Tests to add before implementation: scheduled/on-demand simultaneous refresh; only one authoritative update; revoke/replace/delete/policy config change during network call; revoked stale struct; missing/rotating refresh_token; expiry boundary; refresh failure leaves personal precedence; successful refresh new runtime secret and safe event; invalid ciphertext; disabled policy ignores personal grant only after supplied Person existence/eligibility is validated; stale/deleted/inactive Person never falls back globally. Complete step 4 OAuth matrix with provider success/failure subcases.

Branches/paths validated: no expiry, future expiry, skew threshold, expired active versus explicitly expired, revoked, stale version, provider timeout/401/malformed response, process crash after claim and claim recovery. Follow existing retry/backoff conventions without new permanent server tracking state.

Mocking plan: controllable external HTTP edge using synchronization barriers; real Repo/Oban/Connect. Runtime clock/config via established opts carrier and Zaq.Config where applicable. Documentations to update: refresh module contracts and docs/services/engine.md concurrency, errors and downstream invalidation handoff. >=95% touched-file coverage.

2026-09-14 FINAL USER-APPROVED STORAGE DECISION: canonical grants reuse owner_type/owner_id (org with NULL ID or person with non-null ID) and resource_type=connect_credential/resource_id=credential_id string. Native type/shape and explicit non-null/equality CHECKs plus existing credential_id FK; partial unique org/person slots across statuses. No binding_type, duplicate person_id, extra Person FK, triggers or guard rows. Server derives resource pair and configuration auth fields; secret_binding stays independent. Trusted canonical storage checks literal current active Person, without authenticating callers or resolving aliases. Concurrent orphan grants/secrets are an accepted residual risk. IDs must not be reused operationally; no silent reidentification through stale aliases; synchronous erasure is not guaranteed. Later resolver must check Person exists/eligible BEFORE policy selection even disabled, and missing/stale Person errors NEVER fall back globally. Authenticated writes and OAuth/refresh must recheck current identity; lifecycle cleanup/reconciliation and later distributed server invalidation remain unimplemented in storage task .1.
